cells.remarks: Registers the grant, by the king, of some lands in the village of Tuṅganna in the Raṭṭavāḍi-viṣaya as a brahmadeya, to Śaradaśarmman of the Śāṇḍilya-gotra and the Vājasaneya-śākhā, who was learned in the Vedas and Vedāṅgas and who was a resident of (the village) Garakbhonṇa, for the merit of Achoipoji-Bhaṭṭārika. The inscription was composed by the Sarvadhikṛita Sambapuro-pādhyāya, son of Dharmmachandra, the superintendent of Elephants (hastyadhyaksha) and engraved by Khaṇḍichandra, son of [Ā]ditya-Bhogaka.

cells.date: 1696, Pramadiosha, Appasi 9. su. Friday, dasami, Sadaiyam, (Satabhishaj).
cells.remarks: Registers the settlement made, among the residents including the jelayakkars and the natjar of the 84 villages in the two udayavams of Kuttiyapettai and Pachohaip-perumallur in Sigali-simai—comprising the tract between the Kollidam (Coleroon) and the Kaveri in Soja-mandalam which is said to have been under the authority of the king —to the effect that they would, on behalf of themselves and the king, collect the magamai tax on every kalam of the produce, for the expenses of the sacred bath and offerings of the goddess Periyanayaki-Amman and for repairs in the temple of Tirumani-Alagar at Vadavayuram alias Tirumaiyadi.

cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction ஸ்வஸ்தி ஸ்ரீetc. Registers an agreement by the big assembly of Rajakesari-chaturvēdimangalam, a brahmadēya in Nallur-nādu, which was a subdivision of Nittavinōda-valanādu, to pay all the taxes on certain lands belonging to the Tiruchchohōla-udaiyar-Mahādēva in the interest of the money which they had borrowed from the temple-treasury in the 28th year of Periyadevar who was pleased to take Purvafēśam, Gatigai and Kidāram", for purchasing house-sites, and in the 31st year of Śri-Rājadhirājadeva both of which amounts together with their interest had now accumulated to 710 kaśu. Mentions a kaśu as equivalent to 2 kaśu.

cells.location: Bollavaram, Nandyalkodur taluk, same district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a stone built into the back wall of the ruined temple of Prasannayēśvara
cells.king: Mahārāja Rājādhirāja Śrī-padumahu Nirēh, ruling at 'Anandangarā alias Hasināpuram'.
cells.remarks: Records that Prasannaya, the son of Pāparāju and grandson of Prasannaya of the Kāsyapa-gōtra, Āpastamba-sūtra and Yajus-sākha, born in the family of Gaparāju, the sthānakaṇam of Bollavaram, constructed the temple of Kālī-Viśvanātha and a well near it. On the day of the consecration of the temple and the well he granted some land in the village of Bollavaram and another at Masalaya, son of Virabhadra and granddaughter of Donnamala Lingaballa of the Āpastamba-sūtra and the Mayama-gōtra. Records that the same donor granted some land in the village of Eollavaram as daudya-mānyam to Krishnayya, son of Veňgaya and grandson of Veňkațadri of the Vuesi-shthangōtra, Āpastamba-sūtra and Yajus-sākha, who was the thalakaranan of Prolinkallu. Built in and mutilated. Seems to record a grant of land. Mentions Kasavireddi and Bollavaram and refers to Donnamaris.

text.king: Mahārāja Rājādhirāja Śrī-padumahu Nirēh, ruling at 'Anandangarā alias Hasināpuram'.
text.remarks:
Records that Prasannaya, the son of Pāparāju and grandson of Prasannaya of the Kāsyapa-gōtra, Āpastamba-sūtra and Yajus-sākha, born in the family of Gaparāju, the sthānakaṇam of Bollavaram, constructed the temple of Kālī-Viśvanātha and a well near it. On the day of the consecration of the temple and the well he granted some land in the village of Bollavaram and another at Masalaya, son of Virabhadra and granddaughter of Donnamala Lingaballa of the Āpastamba-sūtra and the Mayama-gōtra.
Records that the same donor granted some land in the village of Eollavaram as daudya-mānyam to Krishnayya, son of Veňgaya and grandson of Veňkațadri of the Vuesi-shthangōtra, Āpastamba-sūtra and Yajus-sākha, who was the thalakaranan of Prolinkallu.
Built in and mutilated. Seems to record a grant of land. Mentions Kasavireddi and Bollavaram and refers to Donnamaris.Read more (1 KB)

cells.place: On a slab set up near the well called Lingabhābhavi. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records that Rudrappayadeva-Mahārāja, the son of Veňkațādripatirāja of Rāmārajya, of the Ātrēya-gōtra and Sūnavamśa, younger brother of the king, granted the village Bollavaram to the god Channaraya of Miraturu. Damaged. Registere's grant (of land) made by Bijjana Cholamahārāja, a feudatory of the king (the 'gift was made into the hands of Ananthasūri-Pandita, the disciple of Nirādzu-nu-l'andita. cells.remarks: Records that Sri Ajutarayāsidha-Siddha-Bhikshuvṛitti Ayyayavaru of the Śrī-Parvata made tax-free the income called Vīramuttappaṇa, to the sthānakaṣ of the temple of Sangamēśvara. Registers the grant of the village Bramhabhatin, son of Bhunktanuni Chitamabhatlu, to the god Sangamēśvara and to the god Mallikārjuna of Srisailam and for feeding brahmanas. The village is said to have been situated in the Mosalimadugu-sīma which was granted to the donor as nayankara by king Achyutaraya-Maharaya.

cells.date: Śaka 1388, Vyaya, Magha, su. 1, dushami, Thursday, Rōhiṇī, Ēka-yōgi, Garuḍa, Simha-lagnam, Gainga-vyāpāra. Kuruha-lagna. [date-calculation appendix, No. 434: 10th year, Simha, śu. trayōdaśi, Friday, Tiruvōṇam = A.D. 1155, August 12, Friday ; ·56 ; ·80.]
cells.remarks: Records that the dam across the Devarasana-kaive which had breached was reconstructed by Vishnapa-Nayaka who bore the title Arivarāya-Todaramalla and who was the Governor of Jagadapratāparāya-Nāyaka, who was in the family of Pralaparudra and of his mother Hasavamba. Mentions his Brahman lieutenant Basavarasa. Eulogises Madad Khan and states that a massive and strong gate at Adatuni and a gate at Sirukopa (i.e., Siruguppa) were built by him.

[date-calculation appendix, No. 461: Śaka 1092, Virōdhi, Chaitra, śu. puṇṇami, Monday, Lunar-eclipse = A.D. 1169, Maroh 14, Friday. There was a lunar-eclipse on this day. The week-day quoted in the inscription is a mistake.]
cells.remarks: Records that Mahāmandalēsvara Tribhuvanavamalla Malli-dēva-Chōla-Mahārāja, son of Irugala and grandson of Govinda of the Chōla family of Oyeyur (i.e. Uraiyur) granted the village Basanur, some lands and some taxes for the daily offerings and worship of the god Nīlakaṇṭha. The chief was governing from his capital at Govindadavapura. It also states that Kēdārisvara-Pandita, son of Sarvēsvara-Pandita was the sthānapati of the temple. The inscription was written by Sivarāma. Records the death of Masavallabhadaya in a battle in a Ballidēvachōļa at Kānneyakallu by the sword of Irugōla.

Mentions the levy of tribute from Tiruvadi (Travancore), the subjugation of Saluva-Nayaka by the king and the planting of a pillar of victory on the banks of the Tamraparani river. The king's star of birth is stated to be Mrigafirasira.
